record.paper_title: Developments and open problems on chiral polytopes
record.original_question: Given regular or chiral (d−1)-polytopes K1 and K2, does there exist a chiral d-polytope whose facets are isomorphic to K1 and whose vertex-figures are isomorphic to K2?

evidence.quote: Problem 31 Given regular (or chiral) (d − 1)-polytopes K1 and K2, does there exist a chiral d-polytope P with faces isomorphic to K1 and vertex-figures isomorphic to K2?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. An abstract d-polytope is a partially ordered set P, with a least element F_{-1} and a greatest element F_d, whose elements (called faces) are graded by a rank function with values in {-1,0,1,...,d}, such that every maximal chain (flag) contains exactly d+2 faces, P is strongly flag-connected, and the diamond condition holds: whenever F < G with rank(G) = rank(F)+2, there are exactly two faces H with F < H < G. The faces of rank d-1 are called facets and, for a vertex v (a face of rank 0), the vertex-figure at v is the section consisting of all faces strictly between v and F_d.

The automorphism group Γ(P) acts on the set of flags of P. The polytope P is called regular if Γ(P) acts transitively on the flags. It is called chiral if Γ(P) has exactly two orbits on the flags such that adjacent flags (flags differing in exactly one face) lie in different orbits; equivalently, P admits all rotational symmetries but no reflective symmetry.

Two abstract polytopes are isomorphic if there is a rank-preserving order isomorphism between them.

Problem. Let K_1 and K_2 be abstract (d-1)-polytopes, each of which is either regular or chiral. Determine necessary and sufficient conditions under which there exists a chiral d-polytope P such that every facet of P is isomorphic to K_1 and every vertex-figure of P is isomorphic to K_2.
artifact.status_search_result: The amalgamation problem for chiral polytopes remains open in general. Partial results are known: it is established that no chiral polytope can have flat finite regular facets and finite regular vertex-figures, and various existence constructions have produced chiral d-polytopes with prescribed facet types (e.g., simplicial facets with alternating or symmetric automorphism groups for d ≥ 5). However, no general characterization of admissible pairs (K_1, K_2) has been obtained.

status_evidence.title: Non-Flat Regular Polytopes and Restrictions on Chiral Polytopes
status_evidence.snippet: No chiral polytope has flat finite regular facets and finite regular vertex-figures.
status_evidence.claim: Restrictions are known on which regular (d-1)-polytopes can serve as facets/vertex-figures of a chiral d-polytope, but no full characterization is known.

status_evidence.title: Chiral extensions of chiral polytopes
status_evidence.snippet: Constructions of chiral d-polytopes whose facets are isomorphic to a prescribed chiral (d-1)-polytope.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial constructions exist; the general amalgamation question for chiral polytopes is treated as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Construction of chiral polytopes of large rank with alternating or symmetric groups
status_evidence.snippet: Existence of chiral d-polytopes with simplicial facets and automorphism groups A_n or S_n for d ≥ 5.
status_evidence.claim: Recent constructions provide families of chiral polytopes with prescribed facet types, supporting that the general problem is being attacked piecewise.
